title: ANSI mode versus native execution on Runtime 2.0
purpose: ANSI and native execution trade-off. The collision; Keep ANSI for correctness; Disable ANSI for native speed; Decide per workload class; Record the decision in the Environment.
accessibleSummary: ANSI and native execution trade-off. The collision; Keep ANSI for correctness; Disable ANSI for native speed; Decide per workload class; Record the decision in the Environment.
longDescription: ANSI and native execution trade-off. The collision; Keep ANSI for correctness; Disable ANSI for native speed; Decide per workload class; Record the decision in the Environment.

nodes.label: Spark 4.x enables ANSI by default
nodes.summary: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, raising errors where 3.5 returned NULL.
nodes.detail: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, raising errors where 3.5 returned NULL.
nodes.whyItMatters: Spark 4.x enables ANSI mode by default, raising errors where 3.5 returned NULL.

evidence.note: Spark 4.x turns ANSI on by default, so operations that returned NULL on Spark 3.5 now raise runtime exceptions.

drill.example: A cast of a non-numeric string to INT raises rather than producing NULL.
failureModes: Logic that depended on silent NULLs fails loudly after the runtime move.

nodes.label: NEE falls back under ANSI
nodes.summary: The native execution engine falls back to JVM Spark whenever ANSI mode is on.
nodes.detail: The native execution engine falls back to JVM Spark whenever ANSI mode is on.
nodes.whyItMatters: The native execution engine falls back to JVM Spark whenever ANSI mode is on.

evidence.note: Structured streaming and ANSI SQL mode always execute on JVM Spark.
An untouched Runtime 2.0 environment with NEE enabled may be running almost entirely on the JVM.

outputs: JVM execution despite the native toggle
drill.example: Every operator runs on the JVM even though the Acceleration tab shows the engine as on.
failureModes: The configuration looks correct while the acceleration it promises never occurs.

nodes.label: Keep ANSI — choose correctness
nodes.summary: Keeping ANSI prioritizes correctness guarantees over native execution speed.
nodes.detail: Keeping ANSI prioritizes correctness guarantees over native execution speed.
nodes.whyItMatters: Keeping ANSI prioritizes correctness guarantees over native execution speed.

evidence.note: Data-quality-critical silver pipelines may prefer ANSI's correctness guarantees.

inputs: Workloads where silent NULLs are unacceptable
drill.example: A conformed silver pipeline keeps ANSI so an invalid cast fails rather than quietly nulling a value.
failureModes: Sizing this workload against native benchmarks over-promises throughput.

nodes.label: Disable ANSI — choose native speed
nodes.summary: Disabling ANSI regains native execution for scan-heavy conformed workloads.
nodes.detail: Disabling ANSI regains native execution for scan-heavy conformed workloads.
nodes.whyItMatters: Disabling ANSI regains native execution for scan-heavy conformed workloads.

evidence.note: Scan-heavy gold aggregations may prefer native vectorized speed over ANSI guarantees.

drill.example: A gold aggregation over trusted silver tables regains native execution with targeted try_cast guards.
failureModes: Disabling ANSI on unconformed data reintroduces the silent NULLs it was protecting against.

nodes.label: Decide per workload class
nodes.summary: The choice belongs to the workload class, not to a single global setting.
nodes.detail: The choice belongs to the workload class, not to a single global setting.
nodes.whyItMatters: The choice belongs to the workload class, not to a single global setting.

evidence.note: The ANSI-versus-native trade-off is a per-workload decision rather than a global one.

processing: Decide per class and revisit as coverage improves
drill.example: Silver and gold Environments carry deliberately different ANSI settings.
failureModes: One global setting is necessarily wrong for one of the two workload classes.

nodes.label: Record it in the Environment
nodes.summary: Recording the decision in the Environment makes it visible and reviewable.
nodes.detail: Recording the decision in the Environment makes it visible and reviewable.
nodes.whyItMatters: Recording the decision in the Environment makes it visible and reviewable.

evidence.note: The choice belongs in the Environment's Spark properties rather than ad hoc in notebooks.

processing: Record it as an Environment Spark property
drill.example: The ANSI decision is visible in the Environment rather than buried in one notebook's first cell.
failureModes: Ad hoc notebook settings drift apart across a team and cannot be audited.

nodes.label: Then prove it in the plan
nodes.summary: Plan suffixes confirm which path actually executed.
nodes.detail: Plan suffixes confirm which path actually executed.
nodes.whyItMatters: Plan suffixes confirm which path actually executed.

evidence.note: Native operators carry suffixes such as *Transformer, which confirm what actually executed natively.

processing: Inspect the plan for native operator suffixes
drill.example: The absence of any native suffix confirms ANSI is forcing full JVM execution.
failureModes: Assuming the intended path is the actual path leaves the trade-off unresolved in practice.

edges.label: The default collides with the engine limitation
Disable ANSI to regain native speed
The decision is recorded per Environment
